answer: River-Notebook Challenge. Each identity must, at registration, answer a freshly generated question whose full solution is committed only as a hash and revealed never; the agent instead submits a compact proof that its answer was derived from private randomness it commits to, and the registry checks the proof against that hash. Because the challenge draws on the unpredictable tide of a public randomness beacon, answers can't be copied or precomputed. An attacker must run a separate solve per identity, paying that compute cost each time—no shortcut, no reuse of a quill once written.
